behaviour: Conflict cards reach the owner through the same card renderer as every other card, in words with no record ids.
When the judge finds a record beyond or contradicting the owner words, plumb adds one second-person line to the request read-back card instead of raising a separate card.
note: Depends on read-back card still existing in v2.

behaviour: Plumb avoids redundant log-head reads, lock churn and unchanged progress writes while keeping durable hash-chained entries and timely reporting.
note: Performance tuning preserving guarantees; not owner-visible behaviour.

behaviour: The commanded request check raises a read-back or question card only for messages that start or change something in the repository own system.
note: Scope filter of the clarify check; related to SR-171 and SR-196.

behaviour: The card pane shows one waiting card at a time with its diagram and steps through cards with Back and Next showing n of m.
Answers returned by the question tool are logged as the owner words with question and options, and never confirm, reject or change a record.
Plumb asks with the Claude Code question tool by default and uses a full-context card only for complex record-changing decisions.
note: Overlaps SR-167 on when a card is required.

behaviour: The agent can store a recommended resolution with a reason for a conflict, which the conflict card shows first without choosing anything.
When the panel runs, the end-of-turn text carries only one short plumb line saying what changed, with cards printed in full only without a panel.
An answered card stops counting as waiting at once, and the panel groups cards as waiting, being processed, blocked and done.
Plumb withdraws cards whose question no longer stands, such as current stale links or fully confirmed read-backs, logging and naming each in one line.
A background judge job withdraws open cards that confirmed records already answer or that duplicate another card, and resolves issues from confirmed records before presenting them.
A clear owner answer to a just-asked question is recorded once with that question, closes its card and raises no new card.
A requirement superseded by another is retired: its history stays, it no longer reaches the owner and its links are not checked as stale.
note: Related to SR-188 and SR-195 retirement.

behaviour: At intent capture plumb names the existing requirements the new intent changes or contradicts so they are superseded or reworded in the same capture.
Stale links, untested linked files and unrecorded pins are caught in the turn that makes them, also for workflow agents, and a merge adding such problems is held.
When the agent reply asks a record-changing question, plumb raises it as a card at turn end so the owner answer is read against it.
note: Possibly narrowed by SR-157 (question tool default); conflict unclear.

behaviour: Only the owner own typed words count as the owner; messages from other sessions, notifications or hook text are logged with origin and never confirm anything.
The edit gate is keyed by session and the prompt digest of the owner message, so a ready check opens the gate it closed and other sessions never hold this one.
The plumb prompt hook reads the owner chat reply to an open conflict card and applies it when it clearly picks one version; agents cannot relay conflict choices.
A request is analysed only when the owner types /plumb clarify; ordinary messages run no request check and close no edit hold.
note: SR-193 supersedes it; SR-196 also closes the gate on intent change.

behaviour: When several cards hinge on one principle plumb asks it once and, after the owner confirmed decision, settles each dependent card from it.
The agent receives the brief, stale links and warnings as text while the owner sees only cards and one plumb line; the intent-card setting is retired.
When no judge can be reached plumb says so once and holds the steps needing it, deciding nothing by rule, while judge-free work continues.
Before raising drift cards plumb checks a requirement is still covered by passing tests and a meaning-kept judgment, then repins silently; cards come only for fundamental change or contradiction.
The local browser workspace lists source-session issues with explanations, evidence and existing actions, and its answers preserve exact-content approval and provenance.
The browser shows an issue referenced diagram-mod artifact as extracted SVG with text alternative and zoom, reporting bad artifacts without executing diagram scripts.
Browser answers queue a follow-up delivered once by the source session next prompt hook, shown as queued or delivered and never as typed approval or repair.
The browser workspace is delivered with independent subagent interaction tests against a real local server, demonstration and screenshots.
note: Delivery process for one task, not durable plumb behaviour.

behaviour: Four queued browser integration defects (stale-link state, invalid button index, left-open card offer, unresolved conflict combination) are fixed with regression tests.
note: Bug-fix batch; behaviours belong to other requirements.

behaviour: Hook watchdog, per-hook, covering-test and judge-in-hook time limits are settings in .plumb/config.yaml with defaults above a loaded machine needs.
The verdict judge asks JEV first and uses its verdict above a calibrated no-false-accept threshold, else the configured judge model; a model verdict never approves an intent.
JEV output form is a setting, yes_no by default with choice allowed, and a calibration from one form is never used for the other.
The default pytest run leaves tests/browser uncollected; naming the directory or passing --browser collects it.
When the verdict cascade answers only some records of a judge job, the answers are applied at once and the rest wait with one line saying why.
The judge_model setting governs verdicts and everything that measures or guards them, including evaluation runs and the calibration fingerprint.
When a message does only part of what the reader looks for, the clear part is applied and only the unclear part is asked again.
When a record is superseded its examples tests are unlinked, tests covering no live example are dropped, and the successor keeps only tests of what it states.
A worktree finds the main checkout prompt log through git common directory so judging and captures there see the owner whole message.
A judgment on a record whose premise is its quote alone carries premise quote-only with the reason, and calibration and jev status count such items.
A judge model supported verdict confirms a proposed requirement or decision on verified owner words when auto-approve is on and thresholds are met, undoable in one press.
On Windows every background plumb process is created without a console window yet still outlives its starter.
Typing /plumb intent opens one interactive loop that clarifies through the question tool, checks answers against confirmed records and passes candidates through one judge gate.
Each intent-loop stage records its outcome and the next stage command refuses to run until the previous stage review gate has passed.
A requirement states one durable observable behaviour under a feature, fixes go under the existing requirement, and the version 2 set replaces the current one.
Outside the intent loop the edit gate closes only when a request or edit would contradict or extend a confirmed record and opens when the loop reaches a clear intent.
In the loop the owner states how they will see the intent working, recorded as a proof plan, and the build is done only once that proof is shown.
